counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span connects elevated TSH to the described skin plaques or biopsy findings.
Plasma zinc is only at the lower end of normal, not clearly deficient.
No raw evidence supports primary hypothyroidism as the cause of the hyperkeratotic, parakeratotic biopsy pattern.
decisive_items: well‐defined hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales
hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, focal subcorneal clefting with keratinocyte necrosis
response.rationale: R3 is directly supported by the plaque morphology and biopsy findings of hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, subcorneal clefting, and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate, which together fit psoriasis. R2 and C1 rely only on elevated TSH and do not explain the skin biopsy; R4 relies on low-normal zinc, which is not diagnostic.

rejected.why: Low-normal zinc is not a definitive deficiency and does not explain the hyperkeratotic plaques or biopsy findings.
Append-only completion of R2 with no new raw support; primary hypothyroidism does not account for the biopsy pattern.
